description.summary: promote xdg_toplevel surfaces above the lock screen

protocol.description:
This protocol allows privileged clients to promote their xdg_toplevel surfaces to be displayed above all other surfaces, including the lock screen.
This is intended for system-level modal overlays such as low-battery warnings or post-update notifications that must remain visible and interactive even when the session is locked.
A client binds treeland_privileged_overlay_manager_v1 and calls add with an xdg_toplevel to promote it to the overlay layer. The client may add multiple surfaces and remove them individually. Destroying the manager removes all tracked surfaces and returns them to their original z-order.
Access control is mandatory. The compositor must restrict binding to this global to trusted system clients only and must validate each add request against the client's privileges.
The key words "must", "must not", "should", "should not", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: treeland_privileged_overlay_manager_v1
interface.description:
A compositor global that promotes xdg_toplevel surfaces to the privileged overlay layer. Each promoted surface is displayed above the lock screen and captures all input events.
The client calls add to promote a surface and remove to demote it. Destroying the manager removes all surfaces that were added through it and returns them to their original z-order below the lock screen.
When the client disconnects, the compositor destroys the manager and cleans up all tracked surfaces automatically.
Warning! This interface exposes highly sensitive capabilities. The compositor must restrict binding to this global object to trusted system clients only (e.g., via Unix group membership, SELinux label, or explicit UID whitelist). Unprivileged clients must be denied access at the bind phase.

entry.name: permission_denied
entry.summary: the client has no permission to create an overlay surface

entry.name: overlay_not_found
entry.summary: the given xdg_toplevel has not been added

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the manager and all tracked surfaces

request.description: Destroys the manager object. All surfaces previously added through add on this manager are removed from the overlay layer and returned to their original z-order. No further requests may be sent on this object after destruction.

request.name: add

description.summary: promote an xdg_toplevel to overlay surface

request.description:
Promotes the given xdg_toplevel surface to the privileged overlay layer. The surface is placed above the lock screen, is exempt from lock-screen hiding, and captures all keyboard and pointer input.
The compositor must strictly verify that the client has sufficient privileges (e.g., system UID, specific capability) to promote a surface; otherwise it must raise a permission_denied error.

request.name: remove

description.summary: remove an xdg_toplevel from the overlay layer

request.description:
Removes the privileged overlay status from the given xdg_toplevel surface. The surface returns to its original z-order below the lock screen.
If the xdg_toplevel has not been added as an overlay surface on this manager the compositor must raise an overlay_not_found error.
